rows.subtopic: Visible reactions with multiple possible causes
rows.description: A young adult notices a colleague suddenly pale or shaking. It may be fear, low blood sugar, illness or shock, so checking on safety and health comes before judging emotions.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: fear, surprise, trust

rows.description: A young professional chooses a warm or composed expression on purpose in a meeting or client call. Deliberate display is a normal social skill, provided it does not turn into constant suppression.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtype: Literal, figurative and posed communication at work [Interpreting]
rows.description: A young professional reads emails and remarks that may be literal, figurative, posed or sarcastic. Checking intent and avoiding assumptions prevents needless conflict.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A young adult in some settings smiles or stays calm to save face or show respect while feeling upset, which may be read as agreement. Direct gentle clarification avoids misunderstandings.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A young professional laughs after a mistake in a meeting, mixing embarrassment and hope of easing tension. Owning the error briefly and moving on shows steadier handling than laughing it off.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: amusement, embarrassment, hope

rows.subtype: Smiling while crying, tears of joy [Interpreting]
rows.description: A young adult at a wedding or a reunion cries and smiles at once, feeling joy, relief and loss together. Mixed displays are ordinary, and a listener can simply ask or share the moment.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: joy, sadness, relief
